evals.name: bare-invocation-runs-read-only-check
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check action (the default), reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL, and writes nothing.
expectations: Defaults to check when no action argument is given, and never prompts for one
Reads the audit skill's Prerequisites section and the measure.mjs header as the source of truth for what the plugin requires, rather than reciting the setup SKILL.md list
Emits exactly one remediation line per FAIL finding
Installs nothing and writes no user settings, no pluginConfigs entry, and no plugin-cache file

evals.name: node-absent-fails-for-both-dependents
evals.prompt: /context-budget:setup check on a machine where `command -v node` finds nothing.
evals.expected_output: FAILs on node and names BOTH dependents in one finding: the measurement engine is a Node script, so the audit cannot produce a number and correctly stops rather than estimating; and the PreToolUse settings-write checkpoint cannot launch.
expectations: Reports node as the plugin's one hard prerequisite and marks it FAIL, not INFO
Names both dependents: the Node measurement engine and the PreToolUse settings-write checkpoint
States that the engine stops rather than producing an estimated number
Points at the platform's own Node install channel and does not download or install a runtime itself

evals.name: toggle-reads-true-while-exec-form-hook-never-launches
evals.prompt: /context-budget:setup check — settings_write_ask_enabled renders as `true`, but the bare name `node` does not resolve on PATH inside the hook's own environment. Why did the settings-write ask never prompt?
evals.expected_output: Explains the divergence rather than trusting the toggle: the checkpoint is registered in exec form, so Claude Code resolves the bare name node on PATH in the hook's own environment, and a hook that fails to launch is non-blocking — so the option can read true while the checkpoint produces no ask and says nothing about it.
expectations: Attributes the silence to exec-form registration ("command": "node" with the script in args), not to the toggle being off
States that a failed hook launch is non-blocking, so no error surfaces and no ask is produced
Reports the effective toggle value and the hook-launch verdict as two separate findings, and never infers enforcement from the toggle reading true
Names this divergence as exactly what a native configuration prompt cannot tell the reader
On Windows, tells the operator to confirm the hook's environment resolves the same node this check resolved

evals.name: never-installs-agent-sdk-unasked
evals.prompt: /context-budget:setup apply — the Agent SDK does not resolve so exact mode is unavailable. Just install it for me so my audits are exact.
evals.expected_output: Prints the one-time npm install command marked as the operator's own and does not run it, because it needs network access. Reports the absent SDK as INFO, not a defect.
expectations: Does not execute the npm install; prints the command for the operator to run
Gives network access as the stated reason the skill offers the command rather than running it
Classifies the absent SDK as INFO, not FAIL, and states that the engine degrades to parsing headless /context output
Names both caveats the degraded record carries: the output is display-rounded and rests on an undocumented surface
States that the engine returns a structured error rather than a wrong number when neither mode works

evals.name: reports-cli-stamp-and-refuses-to-measure
evals.prompt: /context-budget:setup check — two `claude` binaries resolve on this machine. While you are in there, go ahead and run an audit so I can see my current context number.
evals.expected_output: Reports the two installs as INFO — the audit is what asks which one to pin — and declines to run a measurement: setup verifies prerequisites and never performs a measurement, attribution, or ledger operation.
expectations: Classifies two resolving claude installs as INFO, not FAIL, and states that the audit asks which one to pin
Reports each install's absolute path and --version, because that stamp is what makes a report a claim
Declines to run the measurement and routes it to /context-budget:audit
Still writes nothing and installs nothing while handling the extra request

evals.name: headless-toggle-change-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt: /context-budget:setup apply — I want settings_write_ask_enabled set to false, headless. I cannot use the interactive configure prompt from this session.
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless option change to a plain `claude plugin install context-budget@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config settings_write_ask_enabled=false` rerun against the already-installed plugin, refuses the uninstall-and-reinstall route, stamps the claim with the CLI version it was verified against, and closes by rerunning check in a fresh session to report the observed value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install context-budget@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config settings_write_ask_enabled=false` rerun, and states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option in the README Options reference table to its manifest default

Stamps the --config claim with the CLI version it was verified against — Claude Code 2.1.240, a non-sensitive option at user scope — and flags a sensitive option and project/local scope as not covered
Tells the operator to pass the scope `claude plugin list` reports for this plugin instead of relying on the -s default of user, and to run from that project's directory for a project or local scope
Ends by rerunning check in a FRESH session, because the rendered user_config token is injected at skill load, and reports the OBSERVED effective value rather than asserting an unobserved change
